steps.text: Season salmon fillets with lemon pepper, garlic powder, and salt.

Stir soy sauce, brown sugar, water, and vegetable oil together in a small bowl until sugar is dissolved. Place fish in a large resealable plastic bag; add soy sauce mixture, seal, and turn to coat. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.
Place salmon on the preheated grill, and discard marinade. Cook salmon until fish flakes easily with a fork, about 6 to 8 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Salmon
raw_recipe.description: Grilled salmon with a simple soy sauce and brown sugar marinade. The sweet-salty flavors in the marinade complement the rich salmon fillets perfectly.

video.description: Watch this video, and grill your best salmon ever. A simple soy sauce and brown sugar marinade, with hints of lemon and garlic, are the perfect salty-sweet complement to rich salmon fillets. Fresh vegetables and rice are the perfect side dishes.

review.reviewBody: I have one thing that I do every time I cook salmon. I always make a little foil packet for each fillet and close it up, leaving a little room for air to circulate inside. If you bake the foil packets on a cookie sheet at 425 for about 15 minutes (slightly longer depending on number of fillets), the salmon cooks to perfection every time! This is a great recipe to use when preparing salmon in foil packets... it poaches gently in its on juices and always comes out so tender and delicious!

Excellent recipe. Be sure to use plain Lemon Pepper and not Lemon Pepper Seasoning Salt (you will oversalt if you do). If grilling is rained out, this can be baked in a 450 degree oven for 12 minutes, and then broiled for 5 minutes. The soy sauce and brown sugar blend wonderfully with the salmon flavor.

YUM! This is one of the best marinades I have tasted for salmon! I'd rather stay home and make this than pay for salmon at a restaurant with this recipe! The longer you marinate it - the better. I tried grilling this on a bbq - and it came out very good but didn't hold the seasoning in well (even though I wrapped it in foil). The second time, I wrapped it in foil again and broiled it in the oven - and the marinade really stuck. I use both the lemon pepper seasoning AND fresh lemon juice. I will make this recipe over and over again - especially since I live in the great Northwest where salmon is abundant. I think this would taste good with other types of fish also.

If I'm making salmon, I always use this recipe! I used to never eat fish, but this recipe produces salmon so flavorful everyone will love it. We like spicy food so I add a ~3 tablespoons of fiery toasted sesame oil and 1-2 tsp. of Sriracha to the marinade. I follow other reviewers tips and grill on medium heat: skin side down onto tin foil for 6-8 minutes, then flip flesh side onto hot grill. Peel tin foil off which takes the skin with it. Grill for another 6-8 minutes. The fish is very moist and flavorful and the grill marks are so tasty with the caramelized soy sauce.

We were gifted a 36 oz salmon fillet my nephew caught in a southwest Washington St river. He had it flash frozen. When home I thawed it to serve to my family including my 6 and 8 year old grandchildren. Knowing salmon with just lemon (fine with me) would be a hard sell -I tried this recipe. It was gobbled up! I adjusted the amounts to accommodate the larger size but otherwise exactly as written. My husband grilled atop foil. It took between 15 and and 20 minutes- (we left the fillet whole). It was so moist and delicious- thank you!

DELICIOUS! I didn’t grill the fish as instructed but rather baked the fish with the marinade in the oven at 375 covered for 30 minutes then uncovered for 15 minutes. I also added about 1/4 tbsp of teriyaki sauce. My family LOVES it. My boyfriend and kids aren’t used to fresh fish, and are getting used to it. This recipe seems to be the best so far (that they didn’t complain about after).

I have been making this for years and the only change I make is to omit the lemon pepper(personal preference), add1 tablespoon of liquid smoke and everything else as written. Marinated for 3 hours and baked in 450 degree oven for 12 minutes broil for 5 minutes and make a glaze from the marinade using cornstarch. It's the only way my husband likes salmon. Great smokey sweet flavor!

Totally awesome marinade! I added a little minced garlic and ginger to my marinade, it added depth to it. You can’t go wrong with this one. I’ve made it in my Ninja Foodi on the air crisp mode...PERFECT!!!
I used steel head trout. Everything the same. To grill put flesh down on grill cook first and then flip it. The fish stays together better.

Recipe is great, & the grilling guidance invaluable! I'm not big on sweet or teriyaki, so I followed other reviewers guidance: cut sugar in half, left out dry salt, added ~ a thumb of ginger minced finely, and 2t of a hot sauce. It was magical - even an avowed fish-hater liked it. Maybe the long soak makes the difference? And I even forgot the lemon wedges I'd cut up! Thanks so much!

Great Recipe - The only reason I gave it 3 stars is because it's pretty salty and sweet. I guess we are used to more of a basic recipe so you can really still capture the taste the fish. I baked at 450 for 12 min. Broiled for a few more at same rack height. So if you're like us but want to try this, I suggest you either reduce everything a bit OR don't marinate it and just put a sprinkling over the fish while it's baking on occasion OR make the marinade as more of a sauce to pour over after done, so people can gauge how much sweetness they want themselves. ALSO, Bragg's Soysauce is wonderful and a healthier alternative to real soysauce that has the junk in it
Very taste. The marinade can cause flare ups on the grill and there is no shortage of char.
Fantastic flavor, easy to make.

I think it’s better to sprinkle the dry ingredients on AFTER marinating not before. Otherwise they kinda get washed away. (Note that some lemon pepper seasoning has plenty of salt already. ) Put them on the flesh side. Good staple marinade have made many times.
Family said this was good. But not as good as "Balsamic-Glazed Salmon Fillets."
My favorite for 10 plus years

I made this recipe just as written. I cooked it on the grill and had neighbors calling me to ask what i was making and then to ask for some so they can taste it! My kids were down the street and could smell it on the grill and came running home before dinner was finished cooking. This is sooo good!!
Best salmon I’ve ever had. Consider adding wasabi
I’ve been making this for many years now. Everyone loves it, even those who say they don’t like salmon.
I followed it as directed.
